rationale: A three-year cumulation of the archive's already-tested one-year equity-issuance-net-of-R&D signal is essentially a lookback extension, and the three-year change in book equity net of retained earnings is very close to the published composite/net equity issuance anomaly, so the R&D subtraction is doing too little work to make this a distinct test.

Equity issuance plus net debt issuance scaled by assets is the well-documented net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), and since the archive already has both legs separately their sum with an R&D offset is more likely a rediscovery plus arithmetic than a new mechanism.

target_name: Weakest Link Of Cover And Self Funding
rationale: The conjunction is internally consistent (the NEG correctly orients the financing leg so that high values mean self-funded and the positive sign follows), and joining a stock-cover test to a near-orthogonal flow-financing test via a no-compensation MIN is a substantive economic claim rather than a cosmetic blend, though it does inherit correlation with both parent signals.

target_name: Knowledge Cover Of Claims And Burn
rationale: The non-monotonicity diagnosis is legitimate and well-reasoned, but the resulting expression sits directly between two already-tested archive ratios (knowledge stock per liability dollar and knowledge-net-of-burn per claim), differing only by moving the burn term across the fraction bar, so it is likely to be highly collinear with existing results rather than decisive.

Excluding purchased intangibles while adding the unrecorded research stock is a coherent and genuinely new-to-the-archive pair of adjustments, but the resulting quantity is a tangible-plus-knowledge net worth ratio that overlaps materially with the existing knowledge-stock-net-of-debt and pledgeable-collateral signals, capping its expected incremental information.

target_name: Pre Research Earnings Over Risk Weighted Claims
rationale: This simply crosses an already-tested numerator (pre-research earnings over liabilities, embedded in the gen-5 MIN screen) with an already-tested denominator (risk-weighted claims), and any gain from the at·VOL(ib/at) term is hard to distinguish from the known earnings-volatility/low-volatility anomaly rather than the proposed liquidity-buffer channel.
